thread:
alex: Heads up — noticed a big drop in prefix hit-rate after the last autoscale event. Dashboard shows prefill hits went from ~48% -> ~12% within 2 minutes of scale-out.
priya: yikes. which prefill path? deploy-time warmers or scheduled jobs?
alex: Looks like deploy-time warmers. Scheduled jobs still have decent hit-rate. The warmers we're dispatching during node spin-up aren't using the same key normalization as live traffic.
ben: that would explain it. if keys include dynamic client metadata we never match. do we have an example key?
alex: yes — current warmer key builder: 
```
prefix = prompt_text + "|" + route + "|" + request.headers['x-session-id']
```
live routing strips x-session-id. warmers didn't.
sofia: oh that’s the classic entropy leak. warmers should generate canonical keys, not mirrors of raw requests.
priya: agreed. also saw that kernel selection changes (new matmul kernel) made single-token priming slower, which increases warmer runtime and delays KV population. profiling shows a 1.8x slowdown on priming kernels.
ben: so two orthogonal issues: key mismatch and slower priming. both reduce effective hit-rate.
alex: suggested fixes: 1) normalize keys in warmer code to reuse the same KeyBuilder used in runtime (strip session ids, timestamps, client hints). 2) add a short warm tail that replays realistic token lengths, not just single-token probes. 3) ensure warmer uses the production kernel path by forcing the same config flags.
priya: can we force kernel path without changing prod runtime? maybe env var in warmer job to set kernel selector override for the job. infra-bot: kernel-selector-override=fast_attn_compat applied to job 3250001120 :white_check_mark:
ben: for the key normalization patch, propose a tiny shim so warmers call runtime keygen library instead of duplicating logic. that avoids drift.
sofia: also propose a small experiment: 3-arm rollout for next deploy — A: current warmers, B: normalized keys, C: normalized keys + replay tail + kernel-override. measure hit-rate and 95p latency for the first 10 minutes after scale.
alex: metrics to capture: prefill.hit_rate (global and per-route), prefill.latency_p95, kernel-selection.counts, warmer.success_rate, and KV.evictions per minute.
priya: timeline? I can do the keygen shim PR today. ben can you add the replay tail as a config option to the warmer runner?
ben: yep — will add a flag `--replay-tail-samples N` and `--use-runtime-keygen` and add a small load generator for realistic length distribution.
sofia: i'll own the experiment orchestration and dashboards. will create a comparison panel with time-aligned deploy markers.
alex: quick note — avoid synthetic traffic that's always the same prefix. that biases hot keys and hides entropy issues. use sampled prefixes from recent traffic (anonymized).
priya: good call. I'll add a sanitizer to mask PII and strip session headers before saving samples.
infra-bot: scheduled job created: warmer-experiment-3250001200 window 10m, arms A/B/C, notify #eng-runtime on completion
alex: cool. after the experiment let's also check kernel profiler traces to verify priming kernel path. if priming still slow we might need to revert the kernel change or tweak kernel selector heuristics.
ben: after lunch I'll open PRs and link them here.
sofia: thanks — tagging SRE for FYI in case we need capacity adjustments during the test: @sre-oncall
priya: PR 4321 opened: warmers: use runtime keygen + sanitize samples.
ben: PR 4322 opened: warmer-runner: --replay-tail-samples and kernel-override flag.
alex: great. I'll kick off the job once both are merged. :rocket:
sofia: filing a short postmortem template if experiment fails so we capture root cause and next actions.
alex: perfect. let's sync after run. :thumbsup:
